analysis: The recency-weighted reconstruction trial completed successfully but reduced macro validation HR@10 to 0.5125, versus 0.5212 for the preceding model and the historical uniform-history result of 0.535. Electronics improved to 0.375 from the cited 0.325, but this did not produce an aggregate gain. Other category HR@10 values were Movies_and_TV 0.555, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.515, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.605. The result does not support applying this recency supervision across all categories; it suggests a possible category-dependent benefit, without establishing its cause. No held-out test conclusions are available.
code_summary: Four separately trained MultVAE models retain dataset routing. Histories contain unique items weighted by latest-occurrence decay 2**(-age/10), L2-normalized for the encoder. A sum EmbeddingBag feeds a 256-unit tanh encoder and a 64-dimensional Gaussian latent representation; a 256-unit tanh decoder produces item logits. Reconstruction targets reuse the original recency weights, normalized to sum to each row’s unique-item count. Training preserves encoder dropout 0.5, Adam, KL annealing capped at 0.2, checkpoint selection, and early stopping. Inference uses the posterior mean and shared history transformation through the generated predictor. Deterministic fixtures check reconstruction weights, repeated items, empty histories, row mass, and predictor agreement.
